blocks.question: Can I drive with oil in coolant- +
blocks.answer: If oil on dipstick is clean and engine isn't overheating, drive carefully to a garage. If you see milky oil on dipstick, do not drive at all.

blocks.question: Is it worth repairing coolant contamination on an old car- +
blocks.answer: If car worth £2,000-£4,000 and repair is oil cooler (£400-£800) or head gasket (£550-£1,200), yes. If head is cracked (£1,200-£3,500) on a car under £2,000, evaluate scrap. Repair vs replacement

blocks.question: Which engines have the most coolant contamination problems- +
blocks.answer: Based on 2025 data: BMW N47 (1,450 - oil cooler), VW EA189 (1,050 - oil cooler), Mercedes OM651 (1,250 - oil cooler seals), Toyota 2AD-FTV (260 - head gasket). [EM-VERIFIED]

faqs.question: How much does coolant contamination repair cost in the UK- +
faqs.answer: Coolant flush: £100-£300. Oil cooler: £400-£1,000. Head gasket: £550-£1,200. Cylinder head: £1,200-£3,500. Engine replacement: £2,500-£6,500+. Diagnostic: £50-£150. Engine repair cost guide

faqs.question: What causes oil in coolant but not coolant in oil- +
faqs.answer: Oil cooler failure (diesel engines) - oil pressure is higher than coolant pressure, so oil pushes into cooling system. Head gasket can also cause this, but oil cooler is more common on diesels.

faqs.question: What causes milky oil on dipstick- +
faqs.answer: Head gasket failure (most common), cracked cylinder head, or cracked block. Stop driving immediately - coolant destroys bearing lubrication.
